blocks.text: Dear devout readers listen with concentration and devotion, The episode about Bhai Taru Singh1 (a fearless Singh Martyr). Who got Khan Bahadur2 damned in the Dinive Court, By getting his own scalp removed from his head. (1)
lines: Dear devout readers listen with concentration and devotion,
The episode about Bhai Taru Singh1 (a fearless Singh Martyr).
Who got Khan Bahadur2 damned in the Dinive Court,
By getting his own scalp removed from his head.

blocks.text: He being an inhabitant of the Majha region of Punjab, He resided in village Poolha3 in perfect peace and piety. Being a man of resolute, meditative, upright and abstemious disposition, He was known by the name of Taru Singh Nihang. (2)
lines: He being an inhabitant of the Majha region of Punjab,
He resided in village Poolha3 in perfect peace and piety.
Being a man of resolute, meditative, upright and abstemious disposition,
He was known by the name of Taru Singh Nihang.

blocks.text: As the Lahore Nawab neared the end of his tether, He started committing more and more wicked deeds. It was in the year of 1802 of Bikrami Samvat, That Bhai Taru Singh performed an act of supreme sacrifice. Summoning his subjects, the Nawab made an enquiry, Where from did the Singhs manage to get their wherewithal? Neither did they collect any revenue or cultivate their fields, Nor were they known to carry out any business or employment. (4)
lines: As the Lahore Nawab neared the end of his tether,
He started committing more and more wicked deeds.
It was in the year of 1802 of Bikrami Samvat,
That Bhai Taru Singh performed an act of supreme sacrifice.
Summoning his subjects, the Nawab made an enquiry,
Where from did the Singhs manage to get their wherewithal?
Neither did they collect any revenue or cultivate their fields,
Nor were they known to carry out any business or employment.

blocks.text: Whatever they received by way of offerings in their shrines, Had also been banned through a royal decree. Whatever the Singhs, received in charity in the name of Sikh Gurus, That too had been prohibited through his royal orders. (5)
lines: Whatever they received by way of offerings in their shrines,
Had also been banned through a royal decree.
Whatever the Singhs, received in charity in the name of Sikh Gurus,
That too had been prohibited through his royal orders.

blocks.text: Why did they not die of starvation and hunger, When all kinds of provisions had been made scarce. With Mughal troops blockading all the highways, The Singhs were being killed through search and shoot operations. (6)
lines: Why did they not die of starvation and hunger,
When all kinds of provisions had been made scarce.
With Mughal troops blockading all the highways,
The Singhs were being killed through search and shoot operations.

blocks.text: In whatever village was a Singh reported to be residing, He had ordered that village to be razed to the ground.
Singhs, having deserted their country (in desperation), Had they been moving in the guise of starving mendicants. (7)
lines: Singhs, having deserted their country (in desperation),
Had they been moving in the guise of starving mendicants.

blocks.text: He (the Nawab) had eliminated even the relatives of the Singhs, By dragging them out from their underground hideouts. Mughals, being ferocious falcons as compared to the timid quail like Singhs, Mughals had slaughtered the Singhs after nabbing them everywhere. (8)
lines: He (the Nawab) had eliminated even the relatives of the Singhs,
By dragging them out from their underground hideouts.
Mughals, being ferocious falcons as compared to the timid quail like Singhs,
Mughals had slaughtered the Singhs after nabbing them everywhere.

blocks.text: As no human being could survive without taking food, How were the Singhs still alive without any food to feed? How long could a person survive on leafy vegetables alone, How could one remain active even if one managed to survive? (9)
lines: As no human being could survive without taking food,
How were the Singhs still alive without any food to feed?
How long could a person survive on leafy vegetables alone,
How could one remain active even if one managed to survive?

blocks.text: Dohra:

At this, a wicked person let out the (whole) secret, That the Singh were not dying of any starvation. There were the Sikhs residing in their own country, Who fed themselves only after feeding the (fugitive) Singhs. (10)
lines: At this, a wicked person let out the (whole) secret,
That the Singh were not dying of any starvation.
There were the Sikhs residing in their own country,
Who fed themselves only after feeding the (fugitive) Singhs.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Harbhagat Niranjania4 (a rival to the Guru's seat) remarked, That whatever the earlier informer had reported was indeed true. There was no dearth of such devoted Singhs in that country, Who fed themselves only after feeding the (militant) Singhs. (11)
lines: Harbhagat Niranjania4 (a rival to the Guru's seat) remarked,
That whatever the earlier informer had reported was indeed true.
There was no dearth of such devoted Singhs in that country,
Who fed themselves only after feeding the (militant) Singhs.

blocks.text: They were prepared to face starvation and destitution themselves, But they could not bear a Singh suffering for want of food. They could keep themselves warm in winter by sitting around a fire, But they got expensive garments stitched for the fellow Singhs. (12)
lines: They were prepared to face starvation and destitution themselves,
But they could not bear a Singh suffering for want of food.
They could keep themselves warm in winter by sitting around a fire,
But they got expensive garments stitched for the fellow Singhs.

blocks.text: Many of them, whatever little they earned through rigorous labour, They sent their entire earnings to the Singhs (in the wilds). Many others who engaged themselves in making mats and ropes, They also sent their proceeds to Singhs without fail. (13)
lines: Many of them, whatever little they earned through rigorous labour,
They sent their entire earnings to the Singhs (in the wilds).
Many others who engaged themselves in making mats and ropes,
They also sent their proceeds to Singhs without fail.

blocks.text: Even those who were serving at distant places, They also offered all their wages to the Singhs. Even those among them who had gone abroad, Were sending their money to their dear, devout Singhs. (14)
lines: Even those who were serving at distant places,
They also offered all their wages to the Singhs.
Even those among them who had gone abroad,
Were sending their money to their dear, devout Singhs.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Hearing this account, the Nawab shook his head in distress, Remarking that the Khalsa Panth was indeed very formidable. Since the Khalsa could hardly be eliminated by him, God alone had the power to decimate the Khalsa Panth. (15)
lines: Hearing this account, the Nawab shook his head in distress,
Remarking that the Khalsa Panth was indeed very formidable.
Since the Khalsa could hardly be eliminated by him,
God alone had the power to decimate the Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: Thereafter addressing those whom he had called there, The Nawab asked them to identity those harbouring the Singhs, He reiterated to decimate all those in his state, Who had been sending provisions to the militant Singhs. (16)
lines: Thereafter addressing those whom he had called there,
The Nawab asked them to identity those harbouring the Singhs,
He reiterated to decimate all those in his state,
Who had been sending provisions to the militant Singhs.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Upon this, Harbhagat Niranjania made a disclosure, That there was a village Poolha in the Majha region of Punjab. There was a Singh named Taru Singh, engaged in agriculture, Who paid state revenue along with all his fellow villagers. (17)
lines: Upon this,
Harbhagat Niranjania made a disclosure,
That there was a village Poolha in the Majha region of Punjab.
There was a Singh named Taru Singh, engaged in agriculture,
Who paid state revenue along with all his fellow villagers.

blocks.text: After paying his dues and keeping a little bit for himself, He had been sending the rest to the Khalsa Panth Singhs. His mother and sister who lived with him in his home, They also earned some money doing some odd jobs. (18)
lines: After paying his dues and keeping a little bit for himself,
He had been sending the rest to the Khalsa Panth Singhs.
His mother and sister who lived with him in his home,
They also earned some money doing some odd jobs.

blocks.text: Keeping themselves alive on the barest minimum victuals, They covered their frail bodies with course clothes. Offering whatever they could save from their earnings, They reposed their faith in none else than the Singhs. (19)
lines: Keeping themselves alive on the barest minimum victuals,
They covered their frail bodies with course clothes.
Offering whatever they could save from their earnings,
They reposed their faith in none else than the Singhs.

blocks.text: While plugging their ears against the loudly audible Muslim Azan, They made no offerings of any kind to the Muslim or Sultani Pir. Worshipping the Sikh Gurus and praying to the Gurus alone, They were least scared of dying for their faith. (20)
lines: While plugging their ears against the loudly audible Muslim Azan,
They made no offerings of any kind to the Muslim or Sultani Pir.
Worshipping the Sikh Gurus and praying to the Gurus alone,
They were least scared of dying for their faith.

blocks.text: Shunning to have immersion in the sacred Ganges and Yamuna rivers, They were content to take a dip in the Sikhs' sacred pool. Branding Jagannath5 as a Hindu deity with arms maimed, They did not recite hymns in praise of Lord Rama and Krishna. (21)
lines: Shunning to have immersion in the sacred Ganges and Yamuna rivers,
They were content to take a dip in the Sikhs' sacred pool.
Branding Jagannath5 as a Hindu deity with arms maimed,
They did not recite hymns in praise of Lord Rama and Krishna.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Remaining still during the day, while moving at night, They kept themselves unnoticed by the Mughal patrols. Carrying a bundle on their heads, containing provisions, They made those provisions available to the Singhs. (22)
lines: Remaining still during the day, while moving at night,
They kept themselves unnoticed by the Mughal patrols.
Carrying a bundle on their heads, containing provisions,
They made those provisions available to the Singhs.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Mehtab Singh, being another member of the same fraternity, He hailed from a village known by the name Mirankot. Since the day he had beheaded Muslim feudal Massa Ranghar6 , He had escaped into the wilds after deserting his own village. (23)
lines: Mehtab Singh, being another member of the same fraternity,
He hailed from a village known by the name Mirankot.
Since the day he had beheaded Muslim feudal Massa Ranghar6 ,
He had escaped into the wilds after deserting his own village.

blocks.text: Carrying out his raids in local and distant helmets, He supplied provisions to the Singhs through loot and plunder. Always having a band of fifty odd Singhs under his command, He waylaid the people and robbed them of their possessions. (24)
lines: Carrying out his raids in local and distant helmets,
He supplied provisions to the Singhs through loot and plunder.
Always having a band of fifty odd Singhs under his command,
He waylaid the people and robbed them of their possessions.

blocks.text: Beseeching a few for contributions while threatening some others, He had started collecting fixed amounts from the people. Whosoever refused to pay the amount fixed by him, He committed loot and arson at the offender's property. (25)
lines: Beseeching a few for contributions while threatening some others,
He had started collecting fixed amounts from the people.
Whosoever refused to pay the amount fixed by him,
He committed loot and arson at the offender's property.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Addressing the informer Harbhagat Niranjania, the Nawab asked, That the former should produce Mehtab Singh in his court. Mehtab Singh being supported by many other Singhs, The former must take a large battery of Mughal troops. (26)
lines: Addressing the informer Harbhagat Niranjania, the Nawab asked,
That the former should produce Mehtab Singh in his court.
Mehtab Singh being supported by many other Singhs,
The former must take a large battery of Mughal troops.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Bhai Taru Singh, being alone without any supporters, A court official should be sent to summon the latter. The court official be escorted by twenty odd foot-soldiers, Who should escort him safely during their journey. (27)
lines: Bhai Taru Singh, being alone without any supporters,
A court official should be sent to summon the latter.
The court official be escorted by twenty odd foot-soldiers,
Who should escort him safely during their journey.

blocks.text: Carrying out the orders of the Nawab of Lahore, Mughal troops proceeded immediately to take on both the Singhs. Reaching there, the Court official took Bhai Taru Singh into custody, Thus promptly carrying out the orders of the Nawab. (28)
lines: Carrying out the orders of the Nawab of Lahore,
Mughal troops proceeded immediately to take on both the Singhs.
Reaching there, the Court official took Bhai Taru Singh into custody,
Thus promptly carrying out the orders of the Nawab.

blocks.text: As the troops camped at village Bhardana7 after Taru Singh's arrest, Many people rushed to see him after hearing the news. The Mughal official, feeling offended at this intrusion, They started beating the people with the whiplashes. (29)
lines: As the troops camped at village Bhardana7 after Taru Singh's arrest,
Many people rushed to see him after hearing the news.
The Mughal official, feeling offended at this intrusion,
They started beating the people with the whiplashes.

blocks.text: Offering some money by way of bribes to the court officials, The residents of Taru Singh's village had a glimpse of Taru Singh's face. Taru Singh's sister who had been taken into custody along with him, Her the people got released by greasing the palms of officials. (30)
lines: Offering some money by way of bribes to the court officials,
The residents of Taru Singh's village had a glimpse of Taru Singh's face.
Taru Singh's sister who had been taken into custody along with him,
Her the people got released by greasing the palms of officials.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The residents of village Bhardana, being guru's devout Sikhs, They felt outraged at the arrest of their fraternal Gurusikh. They resolved to get Bhai Taru Singh released from custory, Whatever it might cost them in limb and property. (31)
lines: The residents of village Bhardana, being guru's devout Sikhs,
They felt outraged at the arrest of their fraternal Gurusikh.
They resolved to get Bhai Taru Singh released from custory,
Whatever it might cost them in limb and property.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter, having resolved to get Bhai Taru Singh released, They communicated their unanimous decision to Taru Singh. Informing him of their decision to slaughter all the officials, They told him of their decision to desert their village. (32)
lines: Thereafter, having resolved to get Bhai Taru Singh released,
They communicated their unanimous decision to Taru Singh.
Informing him of their decision to slaughter all the officials,
They told him of their decision to desert their village.

blocks.text: Terming the securing of a Singh's release as the noblest task, The declared it hundred times nobler than protecting a cow or a Brahmin. As these Singhs arrived with a resolve to accomplish their task, Bhai Taru Singh prohibited them immediately from such a recourse. (33)
lines: Terming the securing of a Singh's release as the noblest task,
The declared it hundred times nobler than protecting a cow or a Brahmin.
As these Singhs arrived with a resolve to accomplish their task,
Bhai Taru Singh prohibited them immediately from such a recourse.

blocks.text: Declaring that he would never flee from his impending death, Definitely would he offer himself for sacrifice to the Mughals. The Guru had not only sacrificed his own life for the Sikhs, He had sacrificed his sons and garandsons8 as well. (34)
lines: Declaring that he would never flee from his impending death,
Definitely would he offer himself for sacrifice to the Mughals.
The Guru had not only sacrificed his own life for the Sikhs,
He had sacrificed his sons and garandsons8 as well.

blocks.text: It was for the glory and expansion of the Khalsa Panth, That Guru had put an end to his own family line. The Sikhs being the devout followers of the Sikh Gurus, How could he flee from making a sacrifice? (35)
lines: It was for the glory and expansion of the Khalsa Panth,
That Guru had put an end to his own family line.
The Sikhs being the devout followers of the Sikh Gurus,
How could he flee from making a sacrifice?

blocks.text: Dohra:

It was for the preservation of the glory and dignity of the Khalsa Panth, That so many sacrifices were made by the Sikh Gurus. The Guru not only suffered himself and sacrificed his sons, He blamed the Mughals squarely for these sacrifices. (36)
lines: It was for the preservation of the glory and dignity of the Khalsa Panth,
That so many sacrifices were made by the Sikh Gurus.
The Guru not only suffered himself and sacrificed his sons,
He blamed the Mughals squarely for these sacrifices.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Whatever had the Guru professed from his sacred lips, He fulfilled his sacred vow with a supreme sacrifice. The Guru getting himself slaughtered by the fourth Babur9 , Sacrificed his life for the sake of keeping his vow. (37)
lines: Whatever had the Guru professed from his sacred lips,
He fulfilled his sacred vow with a supreme sacrifice.
The Guru getting himself slaughtered by the fourth Babur9 ,
Sacrificed his life for the sake of keeping his vow.

blocks.text: The Guru had ordained whenever the Hindus (Sikhs) wished to regain sovereignty, It would never be regained without making a sacrifice. Whenever the Mughals committed oppression on the Hindus, The Sikhs should hold the Mughals responsible for their sacrifice. (38)
lines: The Guru had ordained whenever the Hindus (Sikhs) wished to regain sovereignty,
It would never be regained without making a sacrifice.
Whenever the Mughals committed oppression on the Hindus,
The Sikhs should hold the Mughals responsible for their sacrifice.

blocks.text: This message which Guru Nanak had given to Guru Angad Dev, Had been passed over to Guru Amardas by Guru Angad Dev, While Guru Amardas had communicated it to Guru Ram Das, Guru Arjun had fulfilled this mandate with his own sacrifice. (39)
lines: This message which Guru Nanak had given to Guru Angad Dev,
Had been passed over to Guru Amardas by Guru Angad Dev,
While Guru Amardas had communicated it to Guru Ram Das,
Guru Arjun had fulfilled this mandate with his own sacrifice.

blocks.text: Thereafter Guru Hargobind and Guru Har Rai carried on, But they did not get an opportunity to make sacrifices. Guru Harkrishan, reaching Delhi after being arrested, Sacrificed after putting the entire blame on the Mughals. (40)
lines: Thereafter Guru Hargobind and Guru Har Rai carried on,
But they did not get an opportunity to make sacrifices.
Guru Harkrishan, reaching Delhi after being arrested,
Sacrificed after putting the entire blame on the Mughals.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur accepted the Guru's mandate gracefully, After contemplating over Guru Nanak's ordained message. The Guru accepted Mughal's persecution voluntarily at Delhi, Getting himself beheaded by the Mughal's oppressives sword. (41)
lines: Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur accepted the Guru's mandate gracefully,
After contemplating over Guru Nanak's ordained message.
The Guru accepted Mughal's persecution voluntarily at Delhi,
Getting himself beheaded by the Mughal's oppressives sword.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The great Guru Gobind Singh, following the glorious tradition, Fulfilled the mendate as ordained by Guru Nanak, the same way. Sacrificing his own life along with those of his whole family. Guru Gobind Singh fulfilled the mandate of Guru Nanak. (42)
lines: The great Guru Gobind Singh, following the glorious tradition,
Fulfilled the mendate as ordained by Guru Nanak, the same way.
Sacrificing his own life along with those of his whole family.
Guru Gobind Singh fulfilled the mandate of Guru Nanak.

blocks.text: The Guru sacrificed his sons at the altar of Goddess of war, Putting the blame squarely on the Mughals for those sacrifices. Both one's ideology and one's progeny cannot be preserved at a time. As two swords cannot be kept in a single sheath. (43)
lines: The Guru sacrificed his sons at the altar of Goddess of war,
Putting the blame squarely on the Mughals for those sacrifices.
Both one's ideology and one's progeny cannot be preserved at a time.
As two swords cannot be kept in a single sheath.

blocks.text: Neither can two sovereigns sit on a single throne at a time, Nor can two rare powers rule at one time in Kaliyuga. At this, the Sikh congregation enquired from Bhai Taru Singh, Which cause made the Sikh Guru's sacrifice their lives? (44)
lines: Neither can two sovereigns sit on a single throne at a time,
Nor can two rare powers rule at one time in Kaliyuga.
At this, the Sikh congregation enquired from Bhai Taru Singh,
Which cause made the Sikh Guru's sacrifice their lives?

blocks.text: Dohra:

Bhai Taru Singh answered the Sikhs' query in the same vein, As was given by the Gurus in their prophetic utterings. How could the truth of the Guru's utterings be effaced, Since it had been ordained by the highest Divine Will. (45)
lines: Bhai Taru Singh answered the Sikhs' query in the same vein,
As was given by the Gurus in their prophetic utterings.
How could the truth of the Guru's utterings be effaced,
Since it had been ordained by the highest Divine Will.

blocks.text: As the Sikh Gurus had made the supreme sacrifice, For the sake of their Sikhs and (the glory of their faith), He being a devout Sikh of those revered Gurus, How could he think of saving his life (at this juncture). (46)
lines: As the Sikh Gurus had made the supreme sacrifice,
For the sake of their Sikhs and (the glory of their faith),
He being a devout Sikh of those revered Gurus,
How could he think of saving his life (at this juncture).

blocks.text: Chaupai:

At this, the Sikh congregation, overawed with such a divination, wondered, What unfortunate moment was it when the Guru had made such a vow? Which exigency had compelled Guru Nanak to make such a pledge, The congregation entreated Bhai Taru Singh to narrate it. (47)
lines: At this, the Sikh congregation, overawed with such a divination, wondered,
What unfortunate moment was it when the Guru had made such a vow?
Which exigency had compelled Guru Nanak to make such a pledge,
The congregation entreated Bhai Taru Singh to narrate it.

blocks.text: When there was no dearth of material assets in the house of Guru Nanak, Why did the Guru choose to renounce the temporal power? As both the powers, material and spiritual, were at His command, As well as the muse as sacred as Saraswati10 flowed from his own lips. (48)
lines: When there was no dearth of material assets in the house of Guru Nanak,
Why did the Guru choose to renounce the temporal power?
As both the powers, material and spiritual, were at His command,
As well as the muse as sacred as Saraswati10 flowed from his own lips.

blocks.text: Guru Nanak, being recipient of the grace of the Divine Lord Himself, The God of sustenance (Vishnu) provided everything to Nanak's House. While Kuber" , the god of wealth served as his storekeeper, The sacred Ganges and Saraswati remained under Guru Nanak's command. (49)
lines: Guru Nanak, being recipient of the grace of the Divine Lord Himself,
The God of sustenance (Vishnu) provided everything to Nanak's House.
While Kuber" , the god of wealth served as his storekeeper,
The sacred Ganges and Saraswati remained under Guru Nanak's command.

blocks.text: At this, Bhai Taru Singh answered the congregation's query, Saying that Guru Nanak alone knew the mystery of his act. It is not for human beings to the extent of his majesty, Since He alone was privy to the mystery of His Divine Will. (50)
lines: At this,
Bhai Taru Singh answered the congregation's query,
Saying that Guru Nanak alone knew the mystery of his act.
It is not for human beings to the extent of his majesty,
Since He alone was privy to the mystery of His Divine Will.
